locale.name: English
rule.R01.name: Exact duplicate entries
rule.R01.template: In {area}, {duplicate_groups:int} sets of identical entries were found ({records_involved:int} entries in all): the same name, relative's name, age, gender and house number. They may be the same person listed more than once.
rule.R02.name: Likely duplicate entries
rule.R02.template: In {area}, {pairs:int} pairs of entries look alike: similarly spelled names, the same relative's name and ages within {max_age_gap:int} years of each other. Some may be the same person listed twice; others may be different people with similar names.
rule.R03.name: Age outside the possible range
rule.R03.template: In {area}, {impossible_ages:int} entries have an age outside the possible range of {min_age:int} to {max_age:int} years on the qualifying date ({under_min:int} below, {over_max:int} above).
rule.R04.name: Age change inconsistent with time elapsed
rule.R04.template: In {area}, {age_jumps:int} electors who appear on both rolls have ages that changed by more than {tolerance:int} year beyond the {elapsed:dec1} years between the two rolls.
rule.R05.name: Unusual deletion rate
rule.R05.template: In {area}, {deletions:int} of the {electors_baseline:int} electors on the earlier roll were deleted ({rate:pct}). Other parts of this constituency deleted about {expected_rate:pct}, so this is {rate_ratio:dec1} times the usual rate. A difference this large is unlikely to be chance alone (q = {q_value}).
rule.R06.name: Unusual addition rate
rule.R06.template: In {area}, {additions:int} new electors were added, equal to {rate:pct} of the earlier roll's {electors_baseline:int} electors. Other parts of this constituency added about {expected_rate:pct}, so this is {rate_ratio:dec1} times the usual rate. A difference this large is unlikely to be chance alone (q = {q_value}).
rule.R07.name: Part appeared or disappeared
rule.R07.template.appeared: {area} appears on the newer roll but not on the earlier one. It has {electors_target:int} electors: {transfers_in:int} moved here from other parts and {additions:int} were newly added.
rule.R07.template.disappeared: {area} was on the earlier roll but has no electors on the newer one. Of its {electors_baseline:int} electors, {transfers_out:int} moved to other parts and {deletions:int} were deleted.
rule.R08.name: Many electors at one address
rule.R08.template: In {area}, up to {max_at_one_address:int} electors are registered at a single house number. In this constituency, 99.9% of house numbers have no more than {threshold:int} electors. {addresses:int} addresses in this part are above that level.
rule.R09.name: Deletions differ sharply between women and men
rule.R09.template: In {area}, {women_deleted:int} of {women_baseline:int} women ({women_rate:pct}) were deleted, compared with {men_deleted:int} of {men_baseline:int} men ({men_rate:pct}). Women per 1,000 men went from {ratio_baseline:int} to {ratio_target:int}. A gap this large between women and men is unlikely to be chance alone (q = {q_value}).
rule.R10.name: Missing or incomplete details
rule.R10.template: In {area}, {missing_fields:int} of {electors_target:int} entries ({missing_share:pct}) are missing a house number or relative's details. In addition, {deletions_unspecified:int} deletions have no recorded reason and {deletions_unrecorded:int} electors disappeared without a deletion entry.
rule.R11.name: Unusual mix of deletion reasons
rule.R11.template: In {area}, {reason_count:int} of {deletions:int} deletions ({reason_share:pct}) were recorded as "{reason:reason}". In other parts of this constituency, that reason accounts for about {expected_share:pct} of deletions (q = {q_value}).
rule.R12.name: Unusual number of first-time voters
rule.R12.template: In {area}, {additions_18_19:int} new electors aged 18 or 19 were added ({rate:pct} of the earlier roll). Other parts of this constituency added about {expected_rate:pct}, so this is {rate_ratio:dec1} times the usual rate (q = {q_value}).
signal.strong: Signal strength: strong. This is very unusual compared with similar parts.
signal.moderate: Signal strength: moderate. This is clearly unusual compared with similar parts.
signal.weak: Signal strength: weak. This is somewhat unusual and is shown to reviewers only.
signal.data_quality: This is a record-level check, not a statistical comparison.
footer: An unusual pattern is a reason to look closer, not proof of wrongdoing. Possible innocent explanations are listed with this finding.
alt.pending_deletion: The repeated entry may already be marked for removal in a later update.
alt.re_registration: Someone may have registered again after moving, before the old entry was removed.
alt.data_entry_repeat: The same form may have been entered twice by mistake.
alt.transliteration_variant: Names are spelled in different ways when written in English, so one person can appear with two spellings.
alt.similar_names: Different people can have very similar names and the same relative's name, especially common names.
alt.family_members: Members of one family can have similar names and close ages.
alt.data_entry_error: The age may have been typed wrongly.
alt.age_other_date: The age may have been recorded against a different qualifying date.
alt.form8_correction: Electors can correct their age through Form 8, so a large change may be a correction.
alt.earlier_error_fixed: An error in the earlier roll may have been fixed.
alt.house_to_house_verification: An intensive or special revision with house-to-house verification can remove many outdated entries at once.
alt.migration: People may have moved away, for example for work or because of redevelopment in the area.
alt.death_record_catch_up: Deaths from earlier years may have been recorded together.
alt.part_reorganisation: Parts may have been reorganised, moving electors between polling stations.
alt.duplicate_cleanup: A drive to remove repeated entries may have taken place.
alt.new_housing: New housing may have been built in the area.
alt.enrolment_drive: An enrolment drive or camp may have registered many people at once.
alt.first_time_voters: Many young people may have turned 18 around the qualifying date.
alt.polling_station_rationalisation: Polling stations are split or merged to keep each under 1,200 electors.
alt.boundary_update: The boundaries of parts may have been updated.
alt.institution: Hostels, care homes, religious institutions and similar places register many electors at one address.
alt.joint_family: Large joint families can live at one address.
alt.placeholder_house_number: A placeholder such as "0" may have been used where the house number was unknown.
alt.marriage_migration: Women often move after marriage and are removed from their earlier address.
alt.targeted_enrolment: A drive to enrol more women or more men may have changed the balance.
alt.small_part: In a small part, a few changes can shift the numbers a lot.
alt.batch_entry_quality: One batch of forms may have been entered with incomplete details.
alt.source_format_issue: Details may have been lost when the data was converted from its source format.
alt.death_registration_drive: A drive to match the roll with death registrations may have taken place.
alt.verification_campaign: A verification campaign may have recorded many electors as absent or shifted.
alt.qualifying_date_effect: There are four qualifying dates a year, so enrolments can bunch up around one of them.
lim.synthetic_data: This finding comes from synthetic demonstration data. It says nothing about any real place or person.
lim.statistical_not_causal: A statistical test shows how unusual a pattern is, not why it happened.
lim.row_evidence_restricted: The individual entries behind this finding are visible only to authorised reviewers.
lim.fuzzy_matching: Name matching is approximate and can pair different people.
lim.reason_codes_as_recorded: Deletion reasons are used as recorded; they have not been checked independently.
lim.within_part_only: This check compares entries within the same part only.
